(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].[https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2026/7/trent-forrest-fenerbahce-de Trent Forrest Fenerbahçe’de!], Fenerbahçe SK He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. ==Early life== Forrest grew up in [[Chipley, Florida]] and attended [[Chipley High School]]. During his high school career, Forrest scored over 3,000 points.{{cite news |last=Crosby |first=Jim |title=The Unconquered Spirit of Trent Forrest |url=https://seminolesweb-8b76.kxcdn.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/The-Unconquered-Spirit-of-Trent-Forrest.pdf |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=Unconquered Magazine |date=December 2019}} As a senior, he led Chipley to a state championship, scoring 26 points in the title game against [[Paxton High School (Florida)|Paxton High School]]. Forrest also participated in [[Amateur Athletic Union]] competition with the Alabama Challenge and Georgia Stars.{{cite web |last=Thomas |first=Bob |title=Chipley Blacktop Courts, Family Hoop Roots Shape Forrest |url=https://seminolesweb-8b76.kxcdn.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Chipley-Blacktop-Courts-Family-Hoop-Roots-Shape-Forrest.pdf |website=[[Florida State Seminoles]] |access-date=March 10, 2020}} He was ranked in the top 50 of his high school class. Forrest signed with [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] because he fell in love with the vision of coach [[Leonard Hamilton]].{{cite news |last=McGahee |first=Wayne |title=True Seminole Trent Forrest set for final FSU home game |url=https://www.waltonsun.com/sports/20200307/true-seminole-trent-forrest-set-for-final-fsu-home-game |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |publisher=Walton Sun |date=March 7, 2020}} Forrest turned down offers from [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]], [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] and [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]].{{cite news |title=Four-star guard Trent Forrest commits to FSU's 2016 basketball recruiting class |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2015/05/05/four-star-guard-trent-forrest-commits-fsus-basketball-recruiting-class/26926551/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=May 5, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:Trent Forrest vs. Florida.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Forrest with [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] in 2018.]] Forrest averaged 4.9 points, 2.7 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.2 steals per game as a freshman, playing backup point guard to [[Xavier Rathan-Mayes]].{{cite news |last=Lewis |first=Dustin |title=Wyatt Wilkes settling into Tallahassee |url=https://www.fsunews.com/story/sports/2017/07/08/wyatt-wilkes-settling-into-tallahassee/462001001/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=FSU News |date=July 8, 2017}} As a sophomore, Forrest finished fifth on the team in scoring with 7.9 points per game and third in rebounding with 4.9 per game, helping Florida State reach the Elite Eight.{{cite news |last=Holcomb |first=Dave |title=Florida State guard Trent Forrest thanks fans on Twitter following Elite Eight loss |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/college/florida-state-guard-trent-forrest-thanks-fans-twitter-following-elite-eight-loss/Qz7sQecHdV0ki4IO2gEz6J/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[Dayton Daily News]] |date=March 25, 2018}} During a game against [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] on November 25, 2018, Forrest had the cartilage torn completely off the bone in his big toe, yet played through pain and did not miss a single game.{{cite news |last=McGahee |first=Wayne |title=Healthy Florida State basketball point guard Trent Forrest ready to lead the Seminoles |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2019/09/26/fsu-basketball-point-guard-trent-forrest-ready-lead-seminoles-devin-vassell-leonard-hamilton/2412413001/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |date=September 26, 2019}} During the 2019 NCAA Tournament, Forrest scored 20 points and had five rebounds in the Sweet 16 loss to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and was named to the West Regional All-Tournament Team.{{cite news |last=Reed |first=Justin |title=Gonzaga's Brandon Clarke, Rui Hachimura named to West Region all-tournament team, Texas Tech's Jarrett Culver Most Outstanding Player |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/mar/30/gonzagas-brandon-clarke-rui-hachimura-named-to-wes/ |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=March 30, 2019}} As a junior, Forrest averaged 9.3 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite news |last=Ferrante |first=Bob |title=Florida State reloads for next run to NCAA Tournament |url=https://apnews.com/af360771cf51443c9c9d9372d89c761c |access-date=March 10, 2020 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 23, 2019}} He graduated from Florida State in December 2019 with a degree in sports management, and he earned the Skip Prosser Award for best scholar-athlete in the ACC since he carried a 3.43 GPA. At the conclusion of the regular season, Forrest was selected to the Second Team All-ACC and to the Defensive Team.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} He averaged 11.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game as a senior.{{cite news |last=Walden |first=Eric |title=Utah Jazz sign rookie free agents Trent Forrest of Florida State, Romaro Gill of Seton Hall |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2020/11/19/utah-jazz-sign-florida/ |access-date=November 19, 2020 |work=[[Salt Lake Tribune]] |date=November 19, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2020–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Forrest signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]] on November 25, 2020.{{cite web |last=Treasure |first=Angie |date=November 25, 2020 |title=Jazz sign Brantley and Forrest to two-way contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-brantley-and-forrest-two-way-contracts |access-date=April 10, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On August 11, 2021, Forrest signed a second two-way contract{{cite web |last=Falk |first=Aaron |date=August 11, 2021 |title=Jazz Re-Sign Trent Forrest to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-re-sign-trent-forrest-two-way-contract |access-date=August 14, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} and on April 10, 2022, his deal was converted into a standard NBA contract.{{cite web |last=Chunga |first=JP |date=April 10, 2022 |title=Utah Jazz convert contract of Trent Forrest |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-convert-contract-trent-forrest |access-date=April 10, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Atlanta Hawks / College Park Skyhawks (2022–2024)=== On August 8, 2022, Forrest signed a two-way contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard Trent Forrest to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-trent-forrest-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2022|access-date=August 8, 2022}} On September 12, 2023, the Atlanta Hawks re-signed Forrest to a two-way contract.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard Trent Forrest to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-trent-forrest-to-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2023|access-date=September 12, 2023}} On February 29, 2024, Forrest's contract was converted to a standard NBA contract by the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Hawks Convert Contract of Trent Forrest|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-convert-contract-of-trent-forrest|website=NBA.com|date=February 29, 2024|access-date=March 1, 2024}} ===Baskonia (2024–2026)=== On August 8, 2024, Forrest signed with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web|title=Trent Forrest, potencia física para la dirección de Baskonia|url=https://www.baskonia.com/trent-forrest-potencia-fisica-para-la-direccion-de-baskonia/|website=Baskonia.com|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=August 8, 2024|language=Spanish}} ===Fenerbahçe (2026–present)=== On July 8, 2026, Forrest signed a 2+1 year contract with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{cite web|title=TRENT FORREST JOINS FENERBAHÇE!|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2026/7/trent-forrest-joins-fenerbahce|date=July 8, 2026|access-date=July 8, 2026|website=fenerbahce.org}} ==Career statistics== || .248 || .748 || 4.1 || 3.3 || 1.6 || .3 || 8.3 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Both his mother, Barbara Lee, and his father, Lester Forrest, played basketball at [[Chipola Junior College]]. His mother is the pastor of the All Things New Worship Center and Forrest played drums in the church. His father is the manager of Gilmore Park for Chipley's recreation department and built the youth basketball program in the town. Forrest has an older brother, Trey, who also played basketball.
